question: A 44-year-old woman comes to the physician because of progressively worsening shortness of breath with exertion and intermittent palpitations over the last 2 months. She has had neither chest pain nor a cough. Her pulse is 124/min and irregular. Physical examination shows a grade 4/6 high-pitched holosystolic murmur that is best heard at the apex and radiates to the back. The murmur increases in intensity when she clenches her hands into fists. The lungs are clear to auscultation. Further evaluation of this patient is most likely to show which of the following findings?

options.opa: Pulmonary artery thrombus on computed tomography scan
options.opc: Obstruction of the right marginal artery on coronary angiogram
options.opd: Reversible area of myocardial ischemia on nuclear stress test
options.ope: Dilation of left atrium on echocardiogram

analysis: The patient presents with symptoms of shortness of breath, palpitations, an irregular pulse, and a holosystolic murmur that increases with hand clenching, suggestive of mitral regurgitation. The murmur radiating to the back indicates possible involvement of the aortic valve. Given these findings, further evaluation is likely to show dilation of the left atrium on echocardiogram, which is a common consequence of chronic mitral regurgitation.
